Hi Marcus —

Thanks for the details and the template — useful to see your expected reference fields. Answers inline below.

1) Intermediary/correspondent: for SEK->EUR we typically use Nordea Bank AB as the cover/intermediary for our EUR pools. SWIFT: NDEASESSXXX (Nordea, Sweden). Typical correspondent charge we see is EUR 8–18 per cover transfer, depending on value and whether banks apply extra routing legs. I’ve attached Nordea_intermediary_terms.pdf which lists routing examples.

2) Fee treatment recommendation: we generally recommend SHA for the initial customer collection leg (keeps customer experience consistent) and OUR for the cover leg to ensure the beneficiary receives the full EUR amount. If you choose OUR on the cover leg, the payer (ScandPay) will instruct the correspondent to debit ScandPay or the sender, which reduces the chance of beneficiary shortfalls. If Nordea or another correspondent inserts an extra intermediary, you can still get a deduction.

3) VAT/tax treatment: banking/correspondent fees are typically VAT-exempt under Swedish/EU rules (financial services exemption). That said, ScandPay processing fees (our service fee or FX markup) are treated as a supply of services and are subject to VAT when applicable; because Redwood is an EU-registered entity, we normally apply reverse-charge where appropriate — but our standard policy is to show VAT on our invoice unless we have a valid EU VAT ID and reverse-charge confirmation. In short: Nordea/intermediary fees = no VAT; ScandPay service fees = may include VAT (we'll either reverse-charge or charge 25% depending on your VAT setup). Please loop in your tax team if you need a formal certificate.

4) MT103/sample: attached is an anonymized MT103 from a recent test flow and a completed copy of your template with the intermediary fields populated.

Operational note: if Redwood prefers to avoid reconciliation complexity caused by occasional correspondent deductions, ScandPay can offer to absorb up to EUR 10 per cover transfer; anything above that we would pass through and itemize on our invoice. If Redwood prefers a firm cap (e.g., we absorb up to EUR X), we can reflect that in the annex and apply a netting adjustment to the monthly settlement.
